approved_scope: Approved as a mission-scoped VALIDATED lesson: Windows and Linux lstat report different error codes (ENOENT vs ENOTDIR) for the same 'path component is a file, not a directory' condition, discovered via a genuine Linux CI failure during the S5-F-06 correction. Scoped to this mission's own cross-platform CI observation; not generalized into a universal claim about all Node.js filesystem APIs or all environments.

evidence.locator: Section 10, 'Root cause of the CI failure': 'On this Windows machine, an ordinary file occupying an ancestor position empirically produces ENOENT... On Linux (the actual GitHub Actions runner), the POSIX-correct behavior for the identical fixture is ENOTDIR... Confirmed by reading the actual Linux CI job logs (gh run view --job <id> --log), not assumed.'

Section 10: 'This was not a safety regression: METADATA_UNAVAILABLE still maps to the same INVALID_OR_UNSAFE fail-closed reconciliation result; only the specific diagnostic label and one test's exact-substring assertion were affected.'

Section 10, 'Correction': 'introduced a second, narrower helper, isUnresolvedPathError (ENOENT or ENOTDIR), used only by the walk-up loop's retry decision. isGenuineAbsenceError (the S5-F-05 function, ENOENT-only) is completely unchanged in meaning and in every other call site.'
